fatal_errors: The proposed control changes both exposure mode and potentially temperature, so it cannot distinguish tribocorrosion synergy from a simple temperature effect.
It misses the observed non-monotonic temperature response, particularly the minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased tribo-layer disruption at 100 °C.
It omits the identically conditioned DS2205 comparator and the HEA's retained L12/B2 microstructure, which are central to the target explanation.
Surface embrittlement and preferential film removal at phase boundaries are asserted without supporting measurements or cited evidence.
The falsification rule requires total loss, wear rate, and corrosion rate all to increase; failure of any one metric would not logically falsify the proposed coupled feedback.
explanation: The hypothesis captures a general tribocorrosion mechanism—sliding-induced depassivation followed by corrosion and mechanically assisted removal—which overlaps with the high-temperature film-rupture component of the target. However, it is too generic to reconstruct the study. It provides none of the defining thermal-shock, electrolyte, temperature, load, frequency, stroke, counter-body, or timing conditions. It also fails to describe the transition from abrasion at 25 °C to stable-film polishing at 50 °C and patchy oxidative or third-body wear at 100 °C. The predicted monotonic acceleration at elevated temperature is inconsistent with the observed 50 °C wear minimum. Its baseline is not matched because isolated exposure and lower temperature alter different variables, and no evidence supports the proposed interphase localization or embrittlement. A discriminating test would hold temperature and mechanics fixed while comparing simultaneous tribocorrosion with separately measured mechanical wear and corrosion contributions, while tracking OCP transients, repassivation, wear volume, and tribo-layer morphology.
